T-type thermocouples and pressure transducers measured refrigerant temperature and pressure at key points, and RTDs with a flowmeter measured the water- side temperature and flow rate. Airflow through the ID coil was measured using a draw- through code tester with humidity and pressure sensors in the ducts. ID and OD chamber conditions were controlled and recorded throughout each experiment. Cooling or heating capacity was calculated using the air-side enthalpy method, and total power was measured by a power meter. Table 14 summarizes measurement uncertainties, and calculated uncertainties of both COP and capacity are less than 5%. The TES-VCS system can operate year-round, supporting space heating and cooling. The six operating modes are illustrated in Figure 57: cooling normal (C-N), cooling TES charge (C-Ch), cooling TES discharge (C-D), heating normal (H-N), heating TES charge (H-Ch), and heating TES discharge (H-D). In each mode, two of the three heat exchangers are active while the third remains idle. The two reversing valves determine which heat exchangers are active and the refrigerant flow direction, allowing six distinct Page 57 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park operational configurations. Two check valves located upstream of the compressor prevent backflow during mode switching, ensuring system stability. Since the PHX has a smaller internal volume than the OD coil, refrigerant imbalance can occur, leading to overcharging or undercharging of the active loop. To address this, the OD-EXV is designed to regulate subcooling, using the OD coil as a refrigerant buffer. Table 2 summarizes the functional roles of each HX and EXV. The ID-EXV and PHX-EXV control superheat and could be replaced with TXVs in practical systems. At the same time, the OD-EXV operates under proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control of subcooling to stabilize refrigerant charge during TES discharge modes. This coordinated EXV control ensures smooth transitions and reliable operation across all six operating conditions.
